tool_schemas.name: get_service_status
tool_schemas.description: Current version per region, health and error rate of a service.

tool_schemas.name: list_deployments
tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.2.9
args.summary: checkout-api has been failing health checks since the latest deploy (v2.3.1). Rollback to the most recent healthy release v2.3.0 was attempted but rejected because v2.3.0 is quarantined due to CVE-2026-4417. checkout-api was therefore rolled back to the next most recent release that was healthy in production, v2.2.9, in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west); rollback verified as fully rolled out. Follow-up: identify root cause of v2.3.1 health check failures and remediate CVE-2026-4417 so a patched version can be deployed forward.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

1. **Investigated deployment history** — latest release v2.3.1 was failing health checks; most recent previously-healthy production release was v2.3.0.
2. **Attempted rollback to v2.3.0** — rejected by the system because that version is quarantined due to CVE-2026-4417.
3. **Rolled back to v2.2.9** (the next most recent release that was healthy in production) — verified as rolled out in all three production regions: us-east, us-west, eu-west.
4. **Opened SEV2 incident INC-0001** — describing the failed health checks, the quarantined v2.3.0 rollback attempt, and the successful rollback to v2.2.9; the on-call engineer has been paged. The incident also notes follow-up work to find the root cause of v2.3.1's failures and to remediate CVE-2026-4417 so a patched version can be deployed forward.

transcript.reasoning_content: First, check deployments history to find the last healthy release. Let me list deployments and maybe service status. I'll call list_deployments first.

transcript.content: The most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0 (the latest, v2.3.1, is unhealthy). Rolling back now:
transcript.reasoning_content: The most recent healthy release in production is v2.3.0. Roll back to it, then create incident. The rollback and incident are dependent in the sense that the incident describes what I did — I can do rollback first, then incident. Actually the incident summary describes the rollback; I could do both but safer to wait for rollback result. But they're independent calls technically. I'll wait for rollback result to accurately describe. Actually I can do them together, but the incident says "rolled back to v2.3.0" — I know that already. But if rollback fails, incident would be wrong. I'll do rollback first.

transcript.content: v2.3.0 is quarantined due to CVE-2026-4417, so I can't roll back to it. The next most recent release that was healthy in production is v2.2.9, which was previously healthy in production, so rolling back to it doesn't require change-manager approval:
transcript.reasoning_content: v2.3.0 is quarantined due to CVE. Next most recent healthy production release: v2.2.9. It was healthy in production previously. Policy: deploying a version never healthy in production requires approval — v2.2.9 was healthy in production, so no approval needed. Rollback to v2.2.9.

transcript.content: Rollback to v2.2.9 succeeded in all three regions. Now opening the SEV2 incident describing what I did:
